q: Which of the following is a famous brand of surveillance equipment?
n: Hikvision makes CCTV cameras, recorders and other video surveillance equipment. Aiphone makes intercoms, and Phelps Dodge makes electrical wires. Source: Hikvision company profile (hikvision.com); Aiphone and Phelps Dodge Philippines product catalogs.

q: Which of the following is a main component of a CCTV system?
n: A CCTV system is built around its cameras and a recorder. The DVR (digital video recorder) or NVR stores and plays back the footage. An inverter and a "protector" are not system components. Source: IEC 62676 (Video Surveillance Systems); Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (Security Systems).

q: It is a type of camera in a CCTV system that has mechanisms for panning, tilting and zooming.
n: A PTZ camera has motorized pan, tilt and zoom mechanisms, remotely controlled to follow subjects over a wide area. Source: IEC 62676 (Video Surveillance Systems); security equipment terminology.

q: An IP camera is a type of digital video camera that receives control data and sends image data via an IP network. What does IP mean?
n: IP stands for Internet Protocol. An IP camera sends video and receives control data over a computer network instead of coaxial cable. Source: IEC 62676-2 (IP Video Transmission); ONVIF Core Specification.

q: Which type of camera is ideal for long range surveillance?
n: Bullet cameras are named after their elongated design which allows these cameras to accommodate a more telescopic style of zoom lens. With such a lens, varifocal bullet cameras can often achieve great image quality even when zoomed in to the max and situated far from the area of interest. In comparison, dome cameras are often used where a wider field of view is needed. Bullet cameras are long cylinders that often have telephoto or varifocal lenses and IR illuminators. They suit long-range views of perimeters and parking areas. Source: IEC 62676-4 (Application Guidelines); manufacturers' camera selection guides.

q: What is the minimum slope for rolled roofing?
n: Mineral-surfaced roll roofing needs a slope of at least 1 unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (1:12). Flatter roofs call for built-up or membrane roofing. Source: International Residential Code, Sec. R905.5.2 (Roll Roofing – Deck Slope); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 7.

q: A type of roof construction that uses layers of bitumen material and ply sheets.
n: Built-up roofing (BUR) is made of alternating layers of bitumen and reinforcing felts or ply sheets, usually topped with gravel or a cap sheet. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual – Membrane Roof Systems (Built-Up Roofing); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 7.

q: A roofing material consisting of individual overlapping elements placed one over the other.
n: Shingles are individual roofing units laid in overlapping courses. Each course laps the one below to shed water. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 7 (Shingle Roofing); NRCA Steep-Slope Manual.

q: Common size of C-purlins used for roofing a residential building.
n: Light-gauge C-purlins for residential roofs are commonly 2" x 3" (50 x 75 mm). Larger 2" x 4" to 2" x 6" sections are used for longer spans. Source: Philippine steel suppliers' C-purlin size tables; Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Roofing – Steel Purlins).

q: It refers to the highest point where the sloping top chords meet.
n: The apex is the highest point of a truss, where the sloping top chords meet. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Truss); Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Roof Framing).

q: Which type of glass can be used for bathroom doors and windows considering privacy?
n: Patterned (figured) glass has a textured surface that obscures vision while letting light through. It is used for bathroom doors and windows where privacy matters. Source: GANA Glazing Manual (Patterned Glass); Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 17.

q: Which type of interlayer is used to increase noise reduction through laminated glass?
n: Laminating glass with PVB is one of the most effective ways to reduce unwanted noise. Laminated glass bonds plies with a polyvinyl butyral (PVB) interlayer. Acoustic-grade PVB damps vibration and improves sound reduction. Source: GANA Laminated Glazing Reference Manual (Acoustic PVB).

q: A type of glass incorporated or used as a building material.
n: Reference for this is the Salvan’s Architectural Building Materials (page 68). Architectural glass is glass made and used as a building material: windows, curtain walls, partitions and so on. Source: GANA Glazing Manual; Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 17.

q: Where is a light directing glass block most ideally installed?
n: Light-directing (prismatic) glass blocks bend incoming daylight toward the ceiling and deep into the room. They work best installed above eye level. Source: Pittsburgh Corning glass block technical guide; Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting (Daylighting).

q: What type of glass is specified when used on a building exterior wall built along the property line?
n: Since it is a building exterior wall built along the perimeter, it is most likely a firewall. Glass blocks can be used in a firewall as long as it has the same fire rating as the firewall. Therefore, it should be a fire-rated glass block. An exterior wall close to the property line must keep its fire rating, so any glazing in it must be fire-rated glass. That stops fire spreading to or from the neighbor. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (exterior wall openings); NBCP Rule VII (fire zones).

q: A lateral load acting on buildings is parallel to the
n: Lateral loads such as wind and earthquake act horizontally, parallel to the ground, unlike gravity loads, which act vertically. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 207 (Wind) and Sec. 208 (Earthquake); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

q: What is provided so that C-purlins on roof framing will not tilt?
n: Purlin cleats are angle or plate brackets fixed to the top chord or rafter. The purlin is bolted to them so it cannot tilt or roll. Sag rods are a different item that controls sag. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Steel Roof Framing); AISI S100 (cold-formed purlins).

q: What is used to connect a steel column to an RCC foundation?
n: A steel column is welded to a base plate. The base plate spreads the column load and is anchored to the concrete footing with anchor bolts. Source: AISC Design Guide 1 (Base Plate and Anchor Rod Design); NSCP 2015, Ch. 5.

q: What component is used when several steel roof truss members intersect?
n: Gusset plates are steel plates bolted or welded at the joints where several truss members meet. They transfer the member forces through the joint. Source: AISC Steel Construction Manual, Part 9 (Gusset Plates); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 6.

q: The effectiveness and strength of a space frame structure is largely due to the
n: Space frames are made of triangulated (tetrahedral) units. A triangle cannot change shape without changing the length of a side, so the frame is rigid and spans in two directions efficiently. Source: Schodek & Bechthold, Structures (Space Frames); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

q: What is the approximate average dead weight of 100mm glass block partition walls in kg/sqm?
n: However, the reference for this is Salvan’s Architectural and Structural Topics (page 59). Take note that 1 Pa is equal to 0.102 kg/sqm. In the list, the weight of a 100mm glass block partition is 862.2 Pa which when multiplied by 0.102 is 87.9 kg/sqm. NSCP gives a 100 mm glass block wall a dead load of about 0.86 kPa, which is roughly 88 kg/sqm. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 204-1 (Minimum Design Dead Loads – Glass Block).

q: What is the approximate average dead weight of a ceiling assembly of 6mm plywood including joists and furrings in kg/sqm?
n: The reference for this is Salvan’s Architectural and Structural Topics (page 59). Take note that 1 Pa is equal to 0.102 kg/sqm. In the list, the weight of a 6mm plywood ceiling assembly is 239.50 Pa which when multiplied by 0.102 is 24.4 kg/sqm. A 6 mm plywood ceiling with joists and furring weighs about 240 Pa, roughly 25 kg/sqm (1 Pa ≈ 0.102 kg/sqm). Source: NSCP 2015, Table 204-1 (Minimum Design Dead Loads – Ceilings).

q: What is the approximate average dead weight of a curtain wall made of aluminum framing and glass in kg/sqme
n: The reference for this is Salvan’s Architectural and Structural Topics (page 59). Take note that 1 Pa is equal to 0.102 kg/sqm. In the list, the average weight of a curtain wall made of aluminum and glass is 718.50 Pa which when multiplied by 9.102 is 73.3 kg/saqm.-. NSCP lists an aluminum-and-glass curtain wall at about 0.72 kPa, which is roughly 74 kg/sqm. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 204-1 (Minimum Design Dead Loads – Curtain Walls).

q: Which type of wall experiences hydrostatic pressure?
n: Hydrostatic pressure affects buildings particularly foundation walls, basement walls and retaining walls. Basement walls retain soil and groundwater. They are designed for lateral earth pressure plus hydrostatic pressure where the water table rises against them. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 206.3 (Soil Lateral Loads and Hydrostatic Pressure); Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering.

q: Which component of paint gives it the power to hide the substrate color?
n: The base is one of the main components of paint and is also commonly referred to as the body of paint. The pigment, such as titanium dioxide, gives paint its opacity or hiding power, so it covers the color of the substrate. The vehicle (binder plus solvent) carries the pigment and forms the film. Source: ASTM D16 (Paint Terminology – Hiding Power); PDCA Painting Standards.

q: SOSS is a famous brand of what?
n: SOSS makes concealed (invisible) hinges, which are mortised into the door edge and jamb and cannot be seen when the door is closed. Source: SOSS Door Hardware product catalog; Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Invisible Hinge).

q: Kenneth & Mock is a famous brand of what?
n: Kenneth & Mock is a Philippine fabricator and supplier of aluminum and uPVC doors and windows. Source: Kenneth & Mock company profile; Philippine Constructors Association directory.

q: Philflex is a famous brand of what?
n: Philflex is a Philippine manufacturer of electrical wires and cables, such as THHN and building wires. Source: Philflex Cables and Wires company profile; Philippine Electrical Code, Part 1, Art. 3.10 (Conductors).

q: Hornitex is a famous brand of what?
n: Hornitex is a German brand of laminate flooring and decorative boards. Source: Hornitex product catalog; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Floor Finishes – Laminate).

q: NELTEX, Emerald and Atlanta are brands of what?
n: Neltex, Emerald and Atlanta are Philippine brands of PVC and PPR pipes and fittings for water supply and drainage. Source: Neltex, Emerald and Atlanta product catalogs; Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (Materials).

q: What do you call the steel plates commonly used to compensate for the dimensional differences of steel members connected in a heavy steel construction?
n: Filler plates (shims or packing plates) fill the gap where connected members differ in thickness, so splices and connections bear properly. Source: AISC 360, Sec. J5 (Fillers); AISC Steel Construction Manual.

q: Steel sheet piles are available in these profiles except what?
n: Steel sheet piles are rolled in interlocking flat (straight-web), U and Z profiles, plus combined H/Z walls. An "L" profile is not a sheet-pile section. Source: ArcelorMittal Piling Handbook; Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Sheet Pile Walls).

q: Which of the following is a vertical component of a typical steel truss framing?
n: The king post is the central vertical member of a truss. It runs from the apex down to the bottom chord. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Truss); Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate.

q: What do you call the metal connection produced by connecting components in molten state?
n: Welding joins metal parts by melting them, usually with a filler metal, into one continuous connection. Source: AWS D1.1 (Structural Welding Code – Steel); Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 11.

q: Which of the following does not describe hot-rolled metal products?
o: Hot-rolled metal products usually have smoother surface than cold-rolled products
Hot-rolled metal products usually have rough surface texture than cold- rolled products
Hot-rolling is generally cheaper than cold-rolling
Hot-rolled metal products have more precise dimensions than cold-rolled products
n: Hot-rolled products cool from high temperature with mill scale. Their surface is rougher and dimensions less precise than cold-rolled products, so saying they are smoother does not describe them. Hot rolling is cheaper. Source: Callister, Materials Science and Engineering; ASTM A6/A6M (tolerances).

q: Single end blocks are most ideal for
n: Single-end (one flat end) CHB units give a finished, flush end at jambs of wall openings. Corners and piers use units that keep the bond. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (CHB Laying); NCMA TEK 14-8.

q: Which of the following building components need bridging?
n: Floor joists are braced with bridging (solid blocking or cross bridging) between them. It keeps the joists from twisting and spreads concentrated loads. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 4 (Wood Joist Framing – Bridging).

q: What type of nail is suggested for installing wooden baseboards?
n: Although brad nail is also a kind of finishing nail, it is more specific. Finishing nails is a more general answer which is the best answer for this question. Finishing nails have small heads that can be set below the wood surface and filled. That suits visible trim such as baseboards. Source: Spence, Carpentry and Building Construction (Nails); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10.

q: In the installation of T&G wood flooring above concrete subfloor, which of the following is needed?
n: Although underlayment is also used to install wood flooring above any surface, the question emphasized the installation of flooring above concrete subfloor. With this, wooden sleepers is the best answer because it directly helps installation of wooden flooring above a concrete subfloor. Over a concrete slab, tongue-and-groove flooring is nailed to wood sleepers anchored to the slab. The sleepers provide nailing and an air space. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10 (Wood Flooring on Concrete Slabs); NWFA Installation Guidelines.

q: What type of roof flashing is installed along the intersection of a firewall and roofing sheet?
n: Apron flashing is installed where a roof meets a vertical wall such as a firewall or parapet. It turns up the wall and laps over the roofing, with counterflashing above. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual (Wall Flashing); Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Flashing).

q: Which of the following is not an elevator company?
n: Schlage makes locks and door hardware. Kone, Fuji and Cibes are elevator and lift manufacturers. Source: Manufacturers' corporate profiles (Allegion–Schlage; KONE; Cibes Lift Group).

q: A retaining wall composed of a stem and a base.
n: A cantilever retaining wall is an L- or inverted-T reinforced concrete wall. Its stem cantilevers from a base slab, which uses the weight of the backfill on the heel for stability. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Retaining Walls); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 1.

q: A retaining wall that only supports a height of up to 3 meters.
n: Gravity walls resist earth pressure by their own mass. They are economical only for low heights, up to about 3 m. Taller walls use cantilever or counterfort types. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Retaining Walls – Gravity Walls).

q: What is required in a pool system to flush out contaminants from a swimming pool filter?
n: Backwashing is a pool term used to describe a filter cleaning method which reverses the flow of water through your filter system. Backwashing reverses the flow through a pool filter to flush trapped dirt and contaminants out to waste. Source: ANSI/APSP-11 (Water Quality in Public Pools); Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (Pools).

q: In what building component is the jacking force applied to?
n: In prestressed concrete, the tendons in a precast beam are tensioned by hydraulic jacks. The jacking force is applied to the beam, through the tendons and anchorages. Source: ACI 318 / NSCP 2015, Ch. 4 (Prestressed Concrete); Nawy, Prestressed Concrete.
